Subject: Post-call: integration + model-routing / policy configuration

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. I wanted to summarize the key outcomes, questions, and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum.

Recap (from our discovery call):
- Primary use case: real-time payment support chat + risk-reduction assistant that annotates transactions.
- Volume profile: ~120 req/s peak, median prompt length ~350 tokens, output ~80-150 tokens.
- SLOs: 95th latency target <200ms for chat; cost-sensitive for non-urgent batch rerank jobs.
- Compliance: data residency in US, SOC2 + audit logs required.

Integration/Architecture items called out:
- SDK setup & auth: We recommended server-side SDK with API keys for Hosted API for initial pilot; long-term SSO/KMS for Private.
- Routing & policy: Need routing rules that prefer low-latency variants for chat; fall back to cost-optimized quantized models for non-LAT-critical requests.
- Structured output / tool calling: We discussed using function/tool calling for transaction enrichment and a strict JSON schema for downstream systems.
- Embeddings / rerankers: Suggest embeddings API for ownership lookup and a lightweight re-ranker for top-K reordering in high-throughput batch jobs.

Open questions we captured:
1) Which endpoints in your platform are latency-critical vs batch? (Priya, can you confirm dev/stage vs prod profiles)
2) Are you able to host a small VPC peering for a Private pilot, or do we start Hosted with US-only routing?
3) Which data retention window is required for logs and embeddings?

Action items / next steps:
- Redwood (Dev): propose a draft routing policy + canary plan for the pilot (target: 6/17). Attachment: acme-redwood-integration-diagram.png (high-level).
- Acme (Priya): confirm environ split (prod vs staging) and latency-critical endpoints by 6/16.
- Redwood (Marissa): send mutual action plan & proposed timeline (attached).

Proposed kickoff: week of 6/22 for technical integration (30-45 min). If that works, I can book — please share preferred windows.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the summary. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups from our side: 

- Latency-critical endpoints: chat support and transaction approval assistant (we need the 95th <200ms). Batch jobs: nightly rerank of the fraud model candidate lists, and weekly embedding creation for customer history.
- VPC/private: we prefer to start with Hosted US-only while we validate functionality. Private/VPC is likely for Q3 if pilot goes well.
- Data retention: Logs for 13 months; embeddings stored for 90 days and encrypted at rest.

Couple of technical questions for your SEs: 
1) For the routing policy, can you provide a sample policy that expresses: prefer hosted-low-latency model in us-west; fallback to quantized model in us-west if load spikes; cross-region fallback to us-east only if both us-west pools are saturated?
2) For tool-calling: can we enforce a strict JSON schema and return a non-200 if the model output doesn't validate? This is important for our downstream parsers.

We can do the kickoff week of 6/22 — mornings PST are best.

Subject: RE: Post-call: integration + model-routing / policy configuration

Hi Alex / Priya — answering the technical asks and sketching a concrete sample routing policy + integration notes. If helpful I can drop a minimal SDK example in the shared Drive.

1) Sample routing policy (pseudocode / policy DSL):
- route_request(request) {
    if request.type == "chat" and request.region == "us-west" and p95_latency_target <= 200ms:
      prefer model_variant: "rw-chat-lowlatency-v1" (hosted, fp16)
    else if request.type == "chat" and host_pool_util(us-west) > 0.75:
      fallback to model_variant: "rw-chat-quantized-v1" (hosted, int8, lower cost)
    else if host_pool_util(us-west) > 0.95 or regional_capacity(us-west) == 0:
      cross_region_fallback to "rw-chat-lowlatency-v1@us-east"
    else if request.type == "batch_rerank":
      route to "rw-rerank-optimized-v1" (dedicated / lower-cost)
  }

Notes: Redwood supports policy tiers (latency, cost, region) and evaluates rules at request admission. Policies can be pinned per-route and inherited by path (e.g., /api/v1/chat uses chat-policy-v1).

2) Enforcing structured output / tool calling:
- You can configure function/tool schemas at model-route level. Redwood will validate model output against the declared JSON schema server-side. If validation fails you can choose policy: (a) mark request as failed and return 4xx; (b) return best-effort with validation warnings in headers; (c) auto-retry with a more deterministic model variant.
- We'll demonstrate option (a) for production-critical parsers.

3) SDK & auth:
- Quickstart: server-side Node SDK example (use API key stored in secret manager). For Hosted pilot: create a scoped API key (chat-only, region:us-west).
- For Private later: we support short-lived mTLS tokens and KMS integrations.

4) Embeddings & rerankers:
- Pattern: compute embeddings in batch (daily) and store encrypted in your vector DB (or use Redwood-managed vectors for pilot). Use a small re-ranker model downstream to re-score top 50 candidates; this reduces calls to the larger chat model.

Attachments / samples uploaded to Drive: sdk-quickstart.md (text), sample-routing-policy.yaml (policy DSL), and an example JSON schema for transaction enrichment.

Let me know if you want an in-person walkthrough in the kickoff. I can prep a 20-min technical runbook + 30-min integration session.

-Dev
